hook: UNDP backs *2* workplace creches for low-income families
hook_b: UNDP backs *2* workplace creches for low-income families
tldr: COWE India and UNDP launched a workplace-based childcare collaboration with two pilot Aveksha day-care centres.

beats.what: The centres in Pashamylaram and Suraram will each give children three meals a day plus early learning.
beats.why: The pilots test whether a centre for low-income families can run on shared funding from industry, CSR and parents.
beats.care: Working parents in industrial areas get on-site childcare; the model, if it works, could spread.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: The launch was at the Aveksha Day Care Centre at the TGIIC-IALA office in Pashamylaram.

qs: How much will parents pay per month?
Can the model work in IT parks, not just industrial estates?

facts.t: *Two* Aveksha centres, Pashamylaram and Suraram, are the UNDP pilots.

steps.e: Run on industry, CSR and parent funding

viz.verdict: A test of whether low-cost creches can pay for themselves

watch: Whether the two pilots can run without grants, as the model aims.

sources.name: Telangana Today
sources.title: COWE India, UNDP launch workplace-based childcare pilot centres in Hyderabad

fact: UNDP backs *two* industrial-area creches in Pashamylaram and Suraram as self-sustaining pilots
twist: An AI tool scans the centres' CCTV and *SMS-alerts* staff within seconds if it spots an unsafe act.
